Chapter 3. The Path to Self-Healing—Auditing and the Process of Recall.
Now that we know how much engrams can affect our lives and drive our struggles, the natural question is—what can we do about them? Is there a way to break free from their hold? That’s where auditing comes in.
Auditing is a thoughtful, step-by-step approach that helps us bring those hidden engrams out into the open. It’s about shining a light on memories that have been quietly influencing how we feel and act, so we can finally understand and release them.
Picture this: auditing usually happens in a calm, distraction-free space. One person is the auditor, and the other is the subject. The auditor isn’t there to judge or analyze—they’re simply a gentle guide, helping the subject navigate their memories. The goal is to recall and really experience the details of painful events, so the analytical mind can rework them, stripping away that heavy emotional charge.
So, how does auditing actually work? Let’s break down the process:
First, you create a safe, peaceful environment—a space where you feel comfortable enough to turn your focus inward and really explore.
Next, the auditor encourages you to recall a specific incident—something that might be linked to the feelings or struggles you’re facing right now.
From there, you’re guided to describe the memory in detail. What did you see, hear, or feel? What emotions came up? There’s no rush, and nothing gets skipped over—even the tough parts.
This isn’t a one-and-done kind of thing, either. You’ll revisit the memory as many times as you need. Each time, you might notice something new, or the emotions tied to the memory might start to lose their grip.
The process continues until you feel a sense of relief—maybe even a genuine resolution. That’s the sign that the engram’s influence is finally starting to fade.
Remember, auditing isn’t about reliving trauma just for the sake of it. It’s about letting your analytical mind take the reins, so you can see these old experiences in a new light. The more you bring these hidden memories out of the dark, the less power they have over you. You might notice that old triggers don’t hit as hard, or that automatic reactions start to loosen their hold.
The beauty of auditing is how accessible it is. You don’t need fancy degrees or high-tech gadgets. All it takes is a bit of courage to look inward, and a supportive partner to walk with you through the process. Respect, patience, and a non-judgmental attitude are key—because healing happens best when we feel safe.
Want a real-life example? Imagine someone who’s always been terrified of public speaking, all because of a childhood embarrassment. Through auditing, they recall that original moment, unpack its details, and come to understand how it’s shaped them. By facing the memory head-on, they’re able to let go of the fear and step up to new challenges with confidence.
Of course, the path isn’t always quick or easy. Some engrams are buried deep, and it can take time to reach them. But every step you take leads to more self-awareness and a little more freedom from the past.
So, here’s the key takeaway: auditing is about giving your analytical mind the chance to guide your life, instead of letting old, reactive patterns run the show. Each memory you revisit and resolve is a step closer to healing—and to being truly in control of your own story.
